stealth: direct — no Tor for local targets (Arti has no loopback route)

strix_findings.title: Broken Function Level Authorization via Client-Supplied Header on /admin
strix_findings.description: The `/admin` endpoint relies solely on a client-supplied HTTP header (`x-admin`) to authorize administrative access. An unauthenticated attacker can supply `x-admin: 1` to bypass authorization checks and access the restricted admin panel.
strix_findings.poc:
1. Send a GET request to `/admin` without headers and observe a 403 Forbidden response.
2. Send a GET request to `/admin` with the header `x-admin: 1` and observe a 200 OK response with administrative panel content.

strix_findings.title: SQL Injection in /item endpoint
strix_findings.description: The `/item` endpoint uses f-string interpolation to construct SQL queries, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary SQL via the `id` parameter.
strix_findings.poc:
1. Send a request to `/item` with a valid ID to establish a baseline.
2. Send a request with `id=1%20AND%201=1` to confirm boolean-based injection.
3. Send a request with `id=1%20AND%201=2` to confirm the negative case.
4. Use a `UNION SELECT` payload to extract arbitrary data.

strix_findings.title: Path Traversal in /file endpoint via name parameter
strix_findings.description: The /file endpoint in the FastAPI application is vulnerable to path traversal due to improper validation of user-supplied input in the 'name' parameter. An attacker can use '../' sequences to read arbitrary files on the server.
strix_findings.poc:
1. Send a GET request to /file?name=../../../../etc/passwd
2. Observe that the server returns the contents of /etc/passwd
